_comment: A curated abbreviation lexicon for descriptor text, with the reasoning that shaped it.
THERE IS NO STANDARD TO ADOPT, and saying so is the first honest move. ISO 4 exists but
abbreviates journal titles; nothing general covers English technical terms. So 'a standard
way' has to mean one shared, checked-in, versioned lexicon applied deterministically --
not an external specification arcviz conforms to.
THE TEST EVERY ENTRY MUST MEET is Daniel's, 2026-09-24: an abbreviation must be
unambiguous WITHIN THE DOMAIN THE READER IS IN, not merely derivable from the word.
'authorization' abbreviates to authz and never to auth, because 'authentication' is
equally common in this exact problem domain. A mechanical shortener produces auth from
both and is wrong in a way nobody notices until a reader takes an authorization credential
for an authentication one -- a security-relevant confusion here, not a cosmetic one. That
is why this is a curated list and not a stemmer: the curation IS the value.
THE ECOSYSTEM'S OWN USAGE IS THE SEED, NOT THE ORACLE. KERI and ACDC abbreviate hard
already (i, s, a, e, d, ri, dt) and vLEI ships QVI, LE, ECR and OOR. Prefer what the
domain already says; coin only where nothing exists. But vLEI also ships AUTH, which
collides with exactly the ambiguity above -- so even the ecosystem's usage is reviewed
rather than copied, and where this file disagrees with an upstream abbreviation it says so
in a `note`.
TIERS, NOT ONE FORM. Each term carries full, medium and short. The render already has
responsive tiers, and shortening to the tersest form at every size throws away room it
has. Abbreviate only as much as the width demands -- progressive disclosure applied to
words. `short` may equal `medium` where no shorter form is safe; that is a statement, not
an omission.
REVERSIBLE AND DISCLOSED. An abbreviation is a lossy render, and posture.md treats
lossiness as a cost paid deliberately rather than absorbed silently, so the full term must
stay one gesture away. Nothing here licenses replacing a term with its short form in a
context the reader cannot expand.
DETERMINISTIC. Same term, same output, every time, so a descriptor does not change shape
between renders of the same DAG.

rules.unambiguous_in_domain: An abbreviation MUST NOT be reachable from two terms that both occur in this domain. This is checked by test, not by eye.
rules.never_shorten_below_medium_without_need: A render uses the longest form that fits. `short` exists for the floor form, not as a default.
rules.case: Lower-case in running descriptor text; the ecosystem's own capitalisation (QVI, LEI, ECR, OOR, AID, SAID, KEL, TEL) is preserved because it is how the domain writes them.

authorization.note: Never `auth`. 'authentication' is equally common in this domain and a reader who takes an authorization credential for an authentication one has made a security-relevant mistake. vLEI's own ECR-AUTH uses AUTH; this lexicon deliberately disagrees with it. Daniel, 2026-09-24.

legal entity.note: vLEI's own LE. Left long at medium because two letters are opaque to a reader outside vLEI.

qualified vLEI issuer.note: The domain's own term; no longer form is more readable to anyone who knows it.

verifiable.note: No safe medium form: `ver` collides with version and `verif` with verification.

registry.note: `reg` at short only; it also reads as register/regulation, which is tolerable at the floor form where context is dense.

issuer.note: Deliberately NOT `iss`, which is one character from `issuee` in a domain where the two are constantly contrasted.

issuee.note: See issuer. The pair is the reason neither gets a three-letter form.
